sources.passage: Working with geographic data can involve a surprisingly high barrier to entry. Before making a map, you may need to install specialized software, learn unfamiliar file formats, or move data between several tools. These requirements make free and open-source geographic information systems (GIS) especially valuable. GIS software helps users organize, analyze, and map data connected to places. GeoLibre is one such system, and it runs directly in a web browser. sources.passage: True AI literacy is not just about using the tool well. It is about developing judgment. Students need to learn not only how to generate answers, but how to question them, verify them, and recognize when a polished response reflects fluency rather than understanding. In that sense, AI literacy should be taught less as a technical skill and more as a reflective discipline. The goal is not to ban AI from learning. It is to make sure that education still rewards the human capacities that matter most: interpretation, calibration, self-awareness, and the ability to recognize when confidence has moved ahead of understanding.
